data.title: India's CtrlS to invest over $1 billion to build data centre in Bihar
data.description:
CtrlS Datacenters on Friday signed a pact with the Bihar state government to invest 100 billion rupees ($1.08 billion) to set up a 150-megawatt data centre in the eastern Indian state.

The pact comes amid a wave of data centre investments in India by companies including HCLTech and L&T for a share of the booming AI infrastructure industry.

Here are some details from the data centre operator's statement:

  • The proposed data centre, located in the state capital of Patna, is expected to be commercially operational by 2029-2030 and create 400 direct jobs

  • "Through the memorandum of understanding, we will bring significant investments into Bihar while creating new employment opportunities and contributing to the region's economic growth," CEO Sridhar Pinnapureddy said

  • The company said in October it would invest 100 billion rupees to build a similar facility in Bihar's Bodh Gaya

  • CtrlS inaugurated a data centre in Patna last month, which currently has a capacity of 12 megawatts

  • The company currently operates 19 data centres in the country and projects a cumulative capacity of 4.4 gigawatts by 2030

($1 = 92.9300 Indian rupees)

data.title: KfW backs EUR-47m geothermal project in Germany
data.description:
November 20 (Renewables Now) - Germany’s state-owned development bank KfW is financing three geothermal drilling operations in Pullach, Bavaria, under a scheme that combines promotional loans with insurance against exploration risks.

The project, developed by municipal company Innovative Energie für Pullach GmbH (IEP), involves an investment of around EUR 47 million (USD 51.5m) and aims to expand the local renewable heat supply.

KfW is providing a promotional loan backed by exploration risk insurance from Munich Re and pro rata debt relief funded by the lender. The necessary funds are provided by the German Federal Government. NORD/LB is financing the project company under the arrangement.

The Pullach project is the first geothermal investment supported through the Germany Fund, KfW noted in the statement. The lender added that seven other projects are currently under assessment, while additional developers have expressed interest in the scheme.

IEP can now launch the Pullach South deep geothermal project and expects to start supplying locally sourced heat to 50,000 people from 2029.

(EUR 1 = USD 1.097)

data.title: Front-quarter prices head for second weekly gain on hydro concerns, higher gas
data.description:
Nordic front-quarter power prices rose on Friday and were set for a second consecutive weekly gain amid a deepening hydro deficit, persistently cold and dry weather forecasts, and firmer European gas prices.

  • The Nordic front-quarter baseload power contract (NSBLQc1) was up €3.90, or 2.9%, at €139.80 per megawatt hour (MWh) as of 1138 GMT

  • The contract was up about 1.5% for the week

  • "High pressure over Europe will keep Atlantic low-pressure activity at bay, and Scandinavia will be under the influence of cold and dry air through the next ten days. The resulting weather will be drier than normal and cold, with below-normal temperatures prevailing until the end of the next week," said LSEG meteorologist Georg Mueller

  • "A change to significantly wetter and milder weather is not likely before December 5," Mueller added

  • Nordic water reserves available 15 days ahead (PCAEC00) were seen at 23.27 terawatt hours (TWh) below normal, the lowest since July 17, compared with 23.01 TWh below normal on Thursday

  • Drier weather and low reservoir levels reduce hydropower availability, tightening the power market and supporting Nordic power prices in the hydropower-reliant region

  • Benchmark Dutch and British wholesale gas prices firmed on Friday morning amid ongoing hostilities in the Middle East, outage extensions at Norwegian gas fields and as colder weather is set to lift demand

  • Germany's year-ahead power contract (TRDEBYc1), Europe's benchmark, was up €3.20, or 2.3%, at €144.70 per MWh

  • In the European carbon market, the benchmark contract fell €0.12, or 0.2% to €81.86 a ton

($1 = 0.91 euros)

Such Meeting will be held for the purpose of considering and, if thought fit, passing the resolution set out in Annex 1 hereto, which will be proposed as an Extraordinary Resolution, in accordance with the provisions of Schedule 6 (Provisions for Meetings of the ETP Securityholders) of the master trust deed originally dated 5 December 2017 as most recently amended on 17 July 2024 and as supplemented by a supplemental trust deed dated 29 April 2026 (the "Trust Deed") made between the Issuer and Apex Corporate Trustees (UK) Limited (the "Trustee") and constituting the Relevant Series.

Capitalised terms used, but not defined, in this Notice shall have the meaning given thereto in the Conditions of the ETP Securities set out therein.

BACKGROUND

On 16 November 2026 the ETP Security Value of the ETP Securities of the Relevant Series fell below 2% of  the Principal Amount.

This notice of meeting is being provided in accordance with Condition 8.5(A)(1) of the ETP Securities.

Condition 8.5(A)(1) provides “If on any Valuation Date (a “Threshold Event Date”) the ETP Security Value falls to less than 2.00 per cent. of the Principal Amount of the ETP Securities… The Issuer shall give notice convening a meeting of the ETP Securityholders on a date not more than 30 calendar days after the Threshold Event Date for the purpose of considering an Extraordinary Resolution which would have the effect of reducing the Principal Amount of the ETP Securities to an amount which is not less than 2.00 per cent of the ETP Security Value as at the time of suspension of redemptions, in which event the suspension will cease only if such Extraordinary Resolution is passed”.

Condition 8.5(A)(2) provides “the Issuer may at any time after the Threshold Event Date, for so long as the ETP Security Value continues to be less than 2.00 per cent. of the Principal Amount of the ETP Securities, suspend the right to request redemption of ETP Securities pursuant to Condition 8.2”.

The Issuer has decided not to exercise its discretion to suspend redemptions of ETP Securities of the Relevant Series in accordance with Condition 8.5(A)(2).

The Issuer is proposing to consolidate the ETP Securities of the Relevant Series into ETP Securities with a proportionately higher value, as detailed below. Such consolidation is reasonably expected to improve the liquidity of the ETPs of the Relevant Series for secondary market investors. The consolidation will also have the effect of reducing the aggregate total Principal Amount (and the related Principal Protection Amount) of the ETP Securities of the Relevant Series, as explained below.

PROPOSED CONSOLIDATION OF THE ETP SECURITIES OF THE RELEVANT SERIES

The Issuer is proposing to consolidate all of the ETP Securities of the Relevant Series into ETP Securities with a proportionately larger ETP Security Value of approximately US$30 per ETP Security (the “Target ETP Security Value”), so that for every ETP Security of the Relevant Series held by an ETP Securityholder, they will hold a smaller number of ETP Securities after the consolidation such that the resulting ETP Security Value is as close as possible to the Target ETP Security Value. The number of ETP Securities resulting from the consolidation relative to the number of ETP Securities before the consolidation (the “Consolidation Ratio”) would be determined by the Issuer by reference to the ETP Security Value of the Relevant Series on a Valuation Date following approval of the Consolidation, as shall be notified to ETP Securityholders, using the following formula:

Consolidation Ratio = Target ETP Security Value / Vt

Where:

Vt  is the ETP Security Value on t; and

t  is the Valuation Date determined and notified by the Issuer in accordance with the Conditions.

The Consolidation Ratio will be rounded down to the nearest full integer. If as a result of the Consolidation of the ETP Securities, an ETP Securityholder would become entitled to a fraction of an ETP Security, the Issuer will redeem such fractional ETP Security. The Issuer will notify the Consolidation Ratio and any resulting fractional shares to ETP Securityholders in accordance with the Conditions no later than two (2) Business Days immediately following Vt. (the “Consolidation”).

ETP Securityholders should be aware that whilst it is not proposed to formally amend the Principal Amount applicable to the Relevant Series proportionate to the Consolidation, the Consolidation will have the effect of reducing the aggregate total value of the Principal Amount (and the related Principal Protection Amount) of the ETP Securities of the Relevant Series as explained in further detail below.

As the Consolidation will result in an ETP Securityholder holding less ETPs (albeit at a proportionately higher ETP Security Value), this will impact the return an investor would be entitled to receive on a Mandatory Redemption, Optional Redemption or Final Redemption (a “Redemption Event”), if the Principal Protection Amount is higher than the Pro-rata Liquidation amount at the time of the Redemption Event (assuming that the same number of ETPs are held at the Redemption Event as held immediately after the Consolidation).

PROPOSAL

The purpose of the Meeting is for the ETP Securityholders to consider and, if thought fit, approve the Consolidation (the "Proposal"):

The Issuer is aware of 2 holders of ETP Securities, together holding 2,000 ETP Securities of the Relevant Series, who have indicated their intention to vote in favour of the Proposal.  Accordingly, if such indications are correct and if no other ETP Securityholders of the Relevant Series choose to vote, it is anticipated that the Proposal will ultimately be approved.

If the Proposal is approved by the Meeting, the Consolidation would become effective on such date as shall be notified to the ETP Securityholders of the Relevant Series by the Issuer.

FORM OF THE EXTRAORDINARY RESOLUTION

The resolution that will be put to the ETP Securityholders of the Relevant Series at the Meeting in order to pass the Proposal is set out in Annex 1 hereto. The Proposal is set out in a single Extraordinary Resolution.

DOCUMENTATION

The Trustee has not been involved in the formulation or negotiation of the Proposal (as defined herein) and, in accordance with normal practice, the Trustee expresses no opinion on the merits of the Proposal (which it was not involved in negotiating) or the Extraordinary Resolution (as set out herein) and no opinion on whether the ETP Securityholders would be acting in their best interests voting for or against the Proposal or the Extraordinary Resolution but on the basis of the information contained in this Notice has authorised it to be stated that it has no objection to the Extraordinary Resolution being submitted to the ETP Securityholders for their consideration. The Trustee makes no representation that all relevant information has been disclosed to the ETP Securityholders in connection with the Proposal in this Notice or otherwise. The Trustee is not responsible for the accuracy, completeness, validity or correctness of the statements made in this Notice or omissions therefrom. Nothing in this Notice should be construed as a recommendation to the ETP Securityholders from the Trustee to vote in favour of, or against, any of the Proposal or the Extraordinary Resolution. The Trustee recommends that the ETP Securityholders take their own independent professional advice on the merits and the consequences of voting in favour of, or against, each of the Extraordinary Resolution and the Proposal.

No person has been authorised to make any recommendation on behalf of the Issuer,  the Trustee or the Issuing and Paying Agent as to whether or how the ETP Securityholders should vote pursuant to the Proposal. No person has been authorised to give any information, or to make any representation in connection therewith, other than those contained herein. If made or given, such recommendation or any such information or representation must not be relied upon as having been authorised by the Issuer, the Trustee or the Issuing and Paying Agent.

This Notice is issued and directed only to the ETP Securityholders of the Relevant Series and no other person shall, or is entitled to, rely or act on, or be able to rely or act on, its contents.

Each person receiving this Notice must make its own analysis and investigation regarding the Proposal and make its own voting decision, with particular reference to its own investment objectives and experience, and any other factors which may be relevant to it in connection with such voting decision. If such person is in any doubt about any aspect of the Proposal and/or the action it should take in respect of it, it should consult its professional advisers.

QUORUM AND VOTING

The provisions governing the convening and holding of the Meetings are set out in Schedule 6 to the Trust Deed (Provisions for Meetings of ETP Securityholders).

Quorum

The quorum required at a meeting called to pass the Extraordinary Resolution is two or more ETP Securityholders or agents present in person holding or representing in the aggregate more than 50 per cent. of the number of the ETP Securities for the time being outstanding.

If a quorum is not present within 15 minutes from the time initially fixed for the Meeting, the Meeting shall be adjourned until such date, not less than 14 nor more than 42 calendar days later at such time and place as the chairman of such meeting (the “Chairperson”) determines (the “adjourned meeting”). If a quorum is not present within 15 minutes from the time fixed for the adjourned meeting, the adjourned meeting will be dissolved. At least 14 calendar days' prior notice of a meeting adjourned through want of a quorum shall be given in the same manner as for an original meeting and such notice shall state the quorum required at the adjourned meeting. The quorum required for any such adjourned meeting will be two or more ETP Securityholders or agents present in person being or representing ETP Securityholders, whatever the number of the ETP Securities so held or represented.

Voting

The provisions for meetings of the ETP Securityholders is set out in Schedule 6 of the Master Trust Deed.  A holder of an ETP Security may appoint a proxy in accordance with the relevant rules and procedures of the Relevant Clearing System.

In order to exercise voting instructions an ETP Securityholder must request the Relevant Clearing System to block the ETPs of the Relevant Series in his own account and to hold the same to the order or under the control of a Paying Agent not later than 48 hours before the time fixed for the Meeting in order to give voting instructions to the relevant Paying Agent in respect of the votes attributable to the blocked Relevant ETP Securities. Unless an ETP Securityholder instructs otherwise, the chairman of the Meeting shall be deemed to be appointed as the ETP Securityholder’s proxy for the Meeting. The Relevant ETP Securities so blocked will not be released until the earlier of (i) the conclusion of the Meeting or, where the Meeting is not quorate, the conclusion of the adjourned meeting; and (ii) in respect of a form of proxy, not less than 48 hours before the time for which the Meeting is convened or the revocation of such form of proxy where notice of such revocation has been given to the relevant Paying Agent.  Any voting instructions received by the Registrar with respect to the Meeting, shall, unless revoked in accordance with the provisions set out herein, remain valid for any adjourned meeting.

Voting instructions must therefore be received by the Registrar by 2:30pm Dublin time on 10 December 2026. The deadlines set by any intermediary, broker, dealer, commercial bank, custodian, trust company or other nominee institution and each Relevant Clearing System for the submission and (in the limited circumstances where permitted) revocation of voting instructions may be earlier than the relevant deadlines specified above. You should check with your relevant custodian or nominee immediately to understand what earlier deadlines are set by your nominee institution or institutions.

Any proxy so appointed or representative so appointed shall so long as such appointment remains in full force be deemed, for all purposes in connection with the relevant meeting or adjourned meeting of the ETP Securityholders, to be the holder of the ETP Securities to which such appointment relates and the holder of the ETP Securities shall be deemed for such purposes not to be the holder or owner, respectively.

Each question submitted to the Meeting shall be decided by a show of hands unless a poll is (before, or on the declaration of the result of, the show of hands) demanded by the chairman, the Issuer, the Trustee or one or more persons representing 2 per cent. of the aggregate number of the ETP Securities outstanding.

Unless a poll is demanded, a declaration by the chairman that a resolution has or has not been passed shall be conclusive evidence of the fact, without proof of the number or proportion of the votes cast in favour of or against it.

If a poll is demanded, it shall be taken in such manner and (subject as provided below) either at once or after such adjournment as the chairman directs. The result of the poll shall be deemed to be the resolution of the Meeting as at the date it was taken. A demand for a poll shall not prevent the Meeting continuing for the transaction of business other than the question on which it has been demanded.

A poll demanded on the election of a chairman or on a question of adjournment shall be taken at once.

On a poll, every such person has one vote in respect of each ETP Security of such Series of ETP Securities so produced or represented by the voting certificate so produced or for which he is a proxy or representative. Without prejudice to the obligations of proxies, a person entitled to more than one vote need not use them all or cast them all in the same way.

To be passed at the Meeting, an Extraordinary Resolution requires a majority of at least 75 per cent. of the votes cast.

An Extraordinary Resolution shall be binding on all the ETP Securityholders, whether or not present at the meeting and each of them shall be bound to give effect to it accordingly. The passing of an Extraordinary Resolution shall be conclusive evidence that the circumstances justify its being passed. The Issuer shall give notice of the passing of an Extraordinary Resolution to ETP Securityholders within 14 calendar days but failure to do so shall not invalidate such an Extraordinary Resolution.

Subject to the quorum for the Meeting being satisfied and the Extraordinary Resolution being passed at the Meeting by a majority of at least 75 per cent. of the votes cast and all relevant documents being executed, the Proposal will become effective and the ETP Securityholders will be notified thereof by the Issuer in accordance with the Conditions.

data.title: BJ's Wholesale Credit Card Settlement Boosts 3Q Operating Results — Company Talk
data.description:
BJ's Wholesale Club's third-quarter selling, general and administrative expenses fell to $696.1 million from $788.2 million a year earlier, aided by a roughly $240 million benefit from a credit card interchange fee litigation settlement in which the company was the plaintiff. data.title: UK Stocks Drift Lower Despite Strong Retail Sales Data
data.description:
BRUSSELS (dpa-AFX) - U.K. stock market's benchmark index FTSE 100 drifted lower and hovered around five-month lows on Friday, hurt by losses in mining, defence and financials sectors. Gains in consumer and healthcare stocks helped limit market's downside.

The undertone was bearish due to tech sell-off across global markets despite Anthropic's record IPO and fairly impressive first outing on Wall Street on Thursday.

The FTSE 100 was down 63.53 points or 0.61% at 10,389.15 about half an hour before noon.

Ithaca Energy tumbled 5.5%. Polar Capital Technology Trust Holdings dropped 5%. Halma, Standard Chartered, Computacenter, Lion Finance, Scottish Mortgage, Metlen Energy & Metals, Babcock International, Pershing Square Holdings, Rolls-Royce Holdings, Alliance Witan, HSBC Holdings, Spirax Group and Weir Group lost 2%-4%.

Balfour Beatty, Aberdeen Group, Diploma, F&C Investment, Informa, JD Sports Fashion, AutoTrader Group, Standard Life, BP and Shell also declined sharply.

Bank stocks Standard Chartered Bank, HSBC Holdings and Barclays lost 3.7%, 2.2% and 1.8%, respectively. Lloyds Banking eased by about 1.2%.

Among miners, Antofagasta dropped about 2.7%. Anglo American Plc, Endeavour Mining, Glencore and Rio Tinto slipped 1%-1.4%.

Reckitt Benckiser moved up 2.15%. Unilever, Haleon, Coca-Cola Europacific Partners, Admiral Group, Airtel Africa, Associated British Foods, Coca-Cola HBC, GSK, British American Tobacco, Smith & Nephew, Bunzl, Diageo, Tesco, Sainsbury (J) and AstraZeneca gained 1%-1.7%.

Data from the Office for National Statistics showed UK retail sales rebounded strongly in October, increasing 0.7% in the month following a 0.6% drop a month earlier. Economists had forecast sales to remain flat.

Excluding auto fuel, retail sales grew unexpectedly by 0.9% month-on-month, offsetting the 0.9% decrease logged in September. Sales were expected to drop 0.1%.

On a yearly basis, retail sales growth accelerated to 2.3% in October from 0.4% in September. Excluding auto fuel, retail sales advanced 2.5% after rising 0.4% a month ago.

In the three months to October, retail sales grew 0.4 percent from the previous three months. Food store volumes rose during this period, while fuel retailers mostly recovered from a decline in the three months to July following a spike in March.

Elsewhere, a monthly survey from the market research group GfK showed that British consumer confidence improved in November as shoppers became more willing to make big-ticket purchases ahead of Christmas. The consumer sentiment index rose to -22 in November from -24 in October.

A report from the GfK gorup showed the UK GfK Consumer Confidence Index rose 2 points to -22 in November, recovering slightly from -24 in October, when it recorded its steepest monthly decline since the COVID-19 pandemic.

UK public sector net borrowing increased less than expected in October, the Office for National Statistics said. The government borrowed GBP 17.0 billion in October, which was up by GBP 0.8 billion from the last year. However, this was below the forecast of GBP 18.0 billion.

Central government debt interest payable climbed GBP 2.8 billion to GBP 11.2 billion in October.

data.title: Euromax Announces Closing of Non-Brokered Private Placement
data.description:
www.euromaxresources.com

VANCOUVER, BC, Nov. 20, 2026 /CNW/ -- Euromax Resources Ltd. (): ("Euromax" or the "Company"), announces today that, further to its news release dated November 3, 2026, it has closed its previously announced non-brokered private placement for aggregate proceeds of  C$5,691,440 (the "Proceeds"), through the issuance of 113,828,800 units of the Company (the "Units"), with each Unit consisting of one common share in the capital of the Company (each, a "Common Share") and one Common Share purchase warrant (each, a "Warrant"), each Unit issued at an offering price of C$0.05 per unit (the "Offering"). Each warrant will entitle the holder to acquire one Common Share at an exercise price of $0.075 per Common Share for a period of two years following the closing of the Offering.

The placees of the Offering include one insider of the Company and other investors (the "Placees").

The Common Shares issued pursuant to the Offering are subject to a hold period of four months and one day from the date of issuance, expiring on March 20, 2027, in accordance with the policies of the TSX Venture Exchange (the "TSXV") and applicable securities laws.

The net proceeds from the sale of the Units will be used as follows:

i.      Office, administration and communications costs – 22%

ii.     Salaries – 34%

iii.    Legal & administrative fees – 14%

iv.    Finance costs – 11%

v.     Project working capital – 9%

vi.    Tax, audit & accounting fees – 10%

As one of the Placees is a related party of Euromax under Policy 5.9 of the TSXV and Multilateral Instrument 61-101 – Protection of Minority Security Holders in Special Transactions ("MI 61-101"), in completing the Offering, the Company relied on the exemptions from the formal valuation and minority approval requirements contained in sections 5.5(b) and 5.7(1)(a) of MI 61-101, respectively.

The Placees included Galena Resource Equities Limited ("Galena"), which prior to closing held 508,954,004 Common Shares, representing approximately 54.30% of the total number of issued and outstanding Common Shares, and following closing holds 609,587,828 Common Shares, representing approximately 57.99% of the total number of issued and outstanding Common Shares. Securities of the Company are held by Galena for investment purposes and in the future, it may discuss with management and/or the board of directors of the Corporation any of the transactions listed in clauses (a) to (k) of Item 5 of Form 62-103F1 – Required Disclosure Under the Early Warning Requirements and it may further purchase, hold, vote (if applicable), trade, dispose or otherwise deal in the securities of the Company, in such manner as it deems advisable to benefit from changes in market prices of the Company's securities, publicly disclosed changes in the operations of the Company, its business strategy or prospects or from a material transaction of the Company.

Following the Offering, there are a total of 1,051,146,323 Common Shares issued and outstanding.

The Offering remains subject to the final acceptance of the TSXV.

This press release is issued in part pursuant to National Instrument 62-103 – The Early Warning System and Related Take-Over Bid and Insider Reporting Issues, which also requires a report to be filed with regulatory authorities in each of the jurisdictions in which the Company is a reporting issuer containing information with respect to the foregoing matters (the "Early Warning Report"). A copy of the Early Warning Report will appear with the Company's filings on the System for Electronic Document Analysis and Retrieval+ (SEDAR+) at www.sedarplus.ca and may also be obtained from Stuart Olley, Partner at Gowling WLG (Canada) LLP +1 403 298 1814.

Euromax has a major development project in North Macedonia and is focused on building and operating the Ilovica-Shtuka gold-copper project.

data.title: Former French PM de Villepin launches 2027 presidential bid
data.description:
Key points:
  • De Villepin joins former premiers Edouard Philippe and Gabriel Attal in crowded centre-right field
  • Former Chirac foreign minister best known for 2003 anti-Iraq war UN speech
  • Recent opinion polls show de Villepin at about 3% in first-round voting intentions

By Michel Rose and Elizabeth Pineau

Former French prime minister Dominique de Villepin announced on Friday that he would run for president in the 2027 election, joining an increasingly crowded field of centrist and centre-right candidates seeking to succeed Emmanuel Macron.

De Villepin, 73, who launched his own political movement last year, said he was running to heal a divided and "rotten" France, attacking what he called the "dead star" of Macron's movement while rejecting both the far right and the far left.

The veteran conservative politician served as prime minister under former President Jacques Chirac from 2005 to 2007 after holding the post of foreign minister. He remains best known internationally for his speech at the United Nations in 2003 opposing the US-led invasion of Iraq.

"There is something like a death instinct hanging over our country," de Villepin told a news conference, in his trademark flowery style. "That is why I am a candidate for the presidential election in 2027."

De Villepin's entry further crowds the centre ahead of the 2027 race, with former prime ministers Edouard Philippe and Gabriel Attal also vying to inherit voters from Macron's camp, while candidates from the traditional left and right compete for a shrinking political space between the far right and far left.

Claiming the political legacy of post-war leader Charles de Gaulle, de Villepin has sought to carve out a distinct place in French politics, presenting himself as a defender of a universalist vision of France and rejecting both the far right's emphasis on preserving a "native France" and what he characterises as the identity politics of Jean-Luc Melenchon's France Unbowed.

He has attracted attention in recent years for his outspoken support for the Palestinian cause and criticism of Israel's military campaign in Gaza, positions that have helped raise his profile beyond traditional conservative circles.

His programme combines calls to reduce inequality and public debt, defend international law and rely more heavily on referendums and negotiations with trade unions, including on pension reform. However, the economic policies underpinning those goals remain largely undefined.

He is seen gathering around 3% of voting intentions for the first round of the April-May election in recent opinion polls.

data.title: Anthropic's super-sized debut, Nvidia China crisis and a GTA heist: The financial week in five charts
data.description:
By Anna Szymanski

Every Friday, Reuters Open Interest (ROI) distills the financial week into five key charts, spotlighting the major trends, surprises and overlooked moves that defined the past five days.

1. SIZE MATTERS

MIKE DOLAN, ROI Finance & Markets Columnist: Anthropic's blockbuster IPO this week crowned a bumper year for US new listings in dollar terms, lifting 2026 IPO proceeds above the 2021 peak.

But as the year ​winds down, the actual number of IPOs in 2026 remains below last year's total and well below the average of the past decade. So while there is still a lot of capital available for new listings, the bar for making the cut has been raised. What this means for the future performance of the latest crop of mega caps remains to be seen.

2. CHIPPED ARMOR

JAMIE MCGEEVER, ROI Markets Columnist: The Nvidia scandal has thrust a blinding spotlight on the US-China “AI arms race.” Washington is tightening curbs on Chinese firms accessing advanced US chips, which Beijing still needs to keep its AI engine going.

For its part, Nvidia says it is effectively shut out of the Chinese market, although a Reuters review found more than $3 billion in Chinese computing projects used its restricted chips. Nvidia’s share price is taking a hit, a beating that actually started well before CEO Jensen Huang resigned, shedding roughly $2 trillion of market cap in around six weeks.

Nvidia's stellar earnings report on Tuesday did little to stem the bleeding, especially given reports that the company is now the subject of a US Securities and Exchange Commission probe.

3. TAPS WIDE OPEN

RON BOUSSO, ROI Energy Columnist: Global benchmark Brent crude prices have fallen more than 20% since the start of the month, settling into a no-war, no-peace range just above $90 a barrel.

Gulf oil production and exports have risen steadily since August, easing pressure on global supplies, even as Middle East tensions have escalated, with multiple Iranian strikes on tankers in recent weeks. The poster child for this shaky new normal is Saudi Arabia. Its October oil output rose above its 2025 average despite continued attacks from Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthi militia on Saudi energy infrastructure.

4. GAME ON

ANNA SZYMANSKI, ROI Editor-in-Charge: Grand Theft Auto VI arrived on Thursday after a 13-year wait and an estimated $1 billion or more in production costs, making it one of the most anticipated video-game releases in history. It is expected to generate billions of dollars in first-week sales, delivering a major boost to the industry.

Its impact may extend beyond retail. Fans booked time off for marathon sessions, turning launch day into an unofficial holiday. Whether this leads to missed deadlines and angry bosses or simply a temporary, much-needed respite for stressed workers remains to be seen.

5. SHENZHEN REALITY CHECK

JAMIE MCGEEVER, ROI Markets Columnist: US President Donald Trump has no shortage of economic troubles — inflation, rising interest rates and the Nvidia scandal, to name a few. But when he met Chinese President Xi Jinping in Shenzhen this week, Xi may well have looked at Trump's hand with envy. China's domestic economy is still struggling with the fallout from the country's real estate bust, business investment is plummeting, and the stock market is down 20% since the summer. The only real bright spot is exports, boosted by tech and AI. But what if the AI bubble deflates?

data.title: The Buckle, Inc. Reports Third Quarter Net Income
data.description:
The Buckle, Inc. () announced today that net income for the fiscal quarter ended October 31, 2026 was $48.0 million, or $0.95 per share ($0.94 per share on a diluted basis).

Net sales for the 13-week fiscal quarter ended October 31, 2026 increased 2.6 percent to $329.2 million from net sales of $320.8 million for the prior year 13-week fiscal quarter ended November 1, 2025. Comparable store net sales for the 13-week fiscal quarter ended October 31, 2026 increased 0.6 percent from comparable store net sales for the prior year 13-week period ended November 1, 2025. Online sales decreased 1.4 percent to $52.2 million for the 13-week fiscal quarter ended October 31, 2026, compared to net sales of $53.0 million for the 13-week fiscal quarter ended November 1, 2025.

Net sales for the 39-week fiscal period ended October 31, 2026 increased 4.3 percent to $937.8 million from net sales of $898.7 million for the prior year 39-week fiscal period ended November 1, 2025. Comparable store net sales for the 39-week period ended October 31, 2026 increased 2.5 percent from comparable store net sales for the prior year 39-week period ended November 1, 2025. Online sales increased 1.1 percent to $144.5 million for the 39-week period ended October 31, 2026, compared to net sales of $142.9 million for the 39-week period ended November 1, 2025.

Net income for the third quarter of fiscal 2026 was $48.0 million, or $0.95 per share ($0.94 per share on a diluted basis), compared with net income of $48.7 million, or $0.97 per share ($0.96 per share on a diluted basis) for the third quarter of fiscal 2025.

Net income for the 39-week fiscal period ended October 31, 2026 was $139.3 million, or $2.75 per share ($2.73 per share on a diluted basis), compared with net income of $128.9 million, or $2.57 per share ($2.55 per share on a diluted basis) for the 39-week period ended November 1, 2025.

Management will hold a live audio webcast at 10:00 a.m. EST today to discuss results for the quarter. To register for the live event, please visit https://buckle.zoom.us/webinar/register/WN_iZVFy_StRI2AfMWfqKCqkg. A replay of the event can be accessed through Buckle’s investor relations website within twenty-four hours after the conclusion of the live event (https://corporate.buckle.com/investor-relations/events).

About Buckle

Buckle is a specialty retailer focused on delivering exceptional service and style through unforgettable experiences. Offering a curated mix of high-quality, on-trend apparel, accessories, and footwear, Buckle is for those living the styled life. Known as a denim destination, each store carries a wide selection of fits, styles, and finishes from leading denim brands, including the Company’s exclusive brand, BKE. Headquartered in Kearney, Nebraska, Buckle currently operates 452 retail stores in 42 states, which includes the opening of two new stores located in Round Rock, Texas and Elizabethtown, Kentucky in fiscal November (after the fiscal quarter ended). As of the end of the fiscal quarter, it operated 450 stores in 42 states compared with 442 stores in 42 states at the end of the third quarter of fiscal 2025.

data.title: Loyalist Announces $1,001,000 Non-Brokered Private Placement
data.description:
(TheNewswire)

Toronto, Ontario – TheNewswire – November 20, 2026 – Loyalist Exploration Limited (“Loyalist” or the “Company”) is pleased to announce a non-brokered private placement consisting of the sale of up to 28,600,000 common shares in the capital of the Company to be issued as “flow-through shares” within the meaning of subsection 66(15) of the Income Tax Act (Canada) (“FT Shares”) at a price of $0.035 per FT Share for gross proceeds of up to $1,001,000 (the “Offering”). The FT Shares will be offered to purchasers in all provinces of Canada pursuant to the “accredited investor” and “minimum amount investment” exemptions under National Instrument 45-106 - Prospectus Exemptions.

The gross proceeds from the sale of the FT Shares will be used to incur eligible “Canadian exploration expenses” that qualify as “flow-through mining expenditures”, as such terms are defined in the Income Tax Act (Canada), on the Company’s Timmins-area projects, which will be renounced to the subscribers of FT Shares with an effective date no later than December 31, 2026.

The Company may pay finder’s fees to eligible finders in connection with the Offering.

All of the securities that will be issued in connection with the Offering will be subject to a hold period expiring four months and one day after the date of issuance. Completion of the Offering is subject to the receipt of all required regulatory approvals, including the approval of the Canadian Securities Exchange.

The securities offered have not been registered under the United States Securities Act of 1933, as amended, and may not be offered or sold in the United States or to, or for the account or benefit of, U.S. persons absent registration or an applicable exemption from registration requirements. This release does not constitute an offer for sale of securities in the United States.

data.title: Garuda Indonesia to Offer More Choice, Flexibility and Value With New Ticket Options in 2027
data.description:
JAKARTA, Nov 20, 2026 - (ACN Newswire) - Garuda Indonesia is set to launch a wider range of ticket options in the first quarter of 2027, giving travellers more choice, greater flexibility and competitive price points tailored to their individual travel needs. The new offering marks a key milestone in the airline's customer-focused transformation, making its full-service experience more accessible to a broader range of travellers.

Under the new structure, passengers will be able to choose from several ticket products, each offering a different combination of benefits, including baggage allowance, seat selection, flexibility to change travel plans and other travel privileges.

For domestic Economy Class, the new products will include Standard, Smart and Flex, while international Economy Class will offer an additional Saver option. Business Class passengers will have a choice of Business and Business Flex.

Each category is designed to accommodate different travel priorities, allowing passengers to choose the combination of benefits and flexibility that best suits their needs and preferences.

The new offering will also make it easier for customers to compare ticket options and understand what is included before making a booking. Previously, certain fare choices were dependent on booking-class availability, particularly during peak travel periods. Under the new structure, Garuda Indonesia aims to make its ticket categories more consistently available, giving travellers clearer choices across different price points.

Garuda Indonesia Director of Transformation Neil Raymond Mills said the initiative reflects the airline's commitment to making its ongoing transformation more meaningful to customers, beyond improvements to its business fundamentals.

"Every journey is different, and so are our customers' priorities. Some value greater flexibility, while others are looking for the right combination of services at a competitive price point. By recognising these differences, we can make the Garuda Indonesia experience more relevant and accessible to a wider range of travellers, while maintaining the distinctive service that defines our airline," Neil said.

The expanded ticket offering is scheduled to launch in the first quarter of 2027, with the new product structure developed in accordance with the prevailing aviation regulatory framework.

The initiative is also expected to strengthen the airline's competitiveness while contributing to a healthier and more sustainable aviation industry.

"For us, the success of this initiative goes beyond introducing new ticket products. It is about ensuring that customers have a clear understanding of what they are choosing and can enjoy a seamless experience across every touchpoint, from booking to boarding. This is an important part of how we are translating our transformation into tangible improvements in the way we serve our customers," Neil concluded.

For more information, please visit: https://www.garuda-indonesia.com/id/en/garuda-indonesia-experience/on-ground/fare-choices
